institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Had all the mandatory courses I needed to take during my 5th BA semester and some more as backup. Interesting courses. Good teaching and high workload according to previous reviews. Less academic and more practical approach. A lot of small classes and more high school feeling. Good ranking in political science. Better/warmer weather than Denmark. An EU/Erasmus destination, thus less worrying about finances and no need to apply for Visas nor having to buy a local sim-card. No GPA or language test requirements. That I got to experience living in a French speaking country and practise to use French after having studied it in school. That UCPH offered free 3 weeks of French language teaching in the summer of 2023 prior to this exchange. Paris had a lot to offer as a tourist destination as well.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: -2 from all the negatives: The difficulty of finding a place to stay, air pollution, noise, "might is right/size matters" traffic where you have to make way for cars and especially busses since they don't hold back thus very difficult to bike, very few bike lanes, "Parisian French arrogant attitude", "Je ne parle que français et pas anglais", high alert/security all the time with tall fences everywhere and having to show ID and your bags every time you enter a building such as Sciences Po, high risk of terror, military guys in uniform and big machine guns making it seem as a war zone, high levels of crime, wild and uncivilized compared to DK, paternalistic, hierarchical, rules everywhere but people don't really follow them, low trust society, bike theft is worse than Copenhagen and you have to lock your bike to something, the nightmare French bureaucracy, being called Monsieur/Madame xxx instead of my actual name, very expensive groceries, country of foie gras. Despite all this, a very good destination with even more positives especially for students, since it is very student friendly compared to Copenhagen/Denmark. Overall the happiest semester I've experienced since I left high school albeit also the most stressful! Therefore 8/10

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Very difficult. NEVER pay anything upfront before you've seen the room/apartment at least through a video call. The only non-profit options for housing (equivalent to almene boliger) are CROUS and Cité Universitaire: CROUS offers the cheapest housing at 400 € per month, but is very difficult to get. Cité Universitaire is very good albeit a bit far from Sciences Po (5 km), but very difficult to get as well with prices from 250-900 € depending on the house. Sciences Po has their own internal private housing website which I used:
https://logements.sciencespo.fr/paris
. AirBnB is always a last option. Links that you can use to find housing:

(only for students)

(roommates)

(place with a lot of offer)

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Sciences Po doesn't own any student housing so there is no option for living "on campus".

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: This is probably the worst part of choosing to go to Paris

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Quite difficult, but managed in the end.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They published the course list way too late to be able to get them "forhåndsgodkendt" in advance. Therefore it was difficult to pick the courses based on only the given info and not being able to change them later only made it more stressful to pick correctly especially since we needed to have certain mandatory courses at the 5th BA semester. Add on top the "first come, first served" approach when registering the courses only made it worse.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could send them e-mails.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all my classes besides one, since they CHANGED THE NAME of it without updating their website. Therefore I couldn't find it and had to choose another less interesting course because of it since it was mandatory. Therefore don't search for the name of the course, but for the code such as "DAFF 25A65" when registering for courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Prepare in advance with backup courses especially if you go on 5th semester BA and have to have mandatory courses. Use the search function of your browser to find the courses through their code to do it as fast as possible. Start with the mandatory courses and then the others.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Way better than UCPH. It was in general less academic and more based on the real world with some courses being more like in DK and academic while others didn't even have any reading. A lot more courses and niche subjects to choose among. They had a lot more resources/money and therefore we could have several assignments during the semester which all counted in our grade instead of the one big 3 person exam in the end in UCPH which is just pathetic. The teachers were also better in general, more motivated. Classes being smaller with seminars being around 28 students compared to the 43 in UCPH and thus more time per student. If everything else is equal, go for the seminars since you'll have more feedback and time with the teacher.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses varied a lot but in general Sciences Po has a very different kind of "level" being a lot more about critical thinking, problem solving/finding solutions, giving our own opinions on issues, oral presentations, exams without any notes and therefore requires that you can remember thing by heart etc. While there was less the high level of focus on the syllabus with strict requirements for citation and references and always having the syllabus as your reference/anchoring point when writing in UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I loved it. See above. Also Sciences Po was way less quantitative compared to UCPH. A lot more assignments during the semester. Workload about 2x UCPH. Prepare to spend your whole November and December on just attending your courses, all of which are mandatory and finishing your assignments and presentations. No free time in this period especially if you plan to read the syllabus. Therefore if possible choose your presentation dates as early in the semester as possible id you want to spread the workload instead of it all being in the end since the semester is only 12 weeks and very compact as such. But you'll appreciate having holidays for 1,5 months afterwards.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ASPO 25A11 - Comparative Politics, ASPO 25A23 - International Wars and Conflicts, DAFF 25A65 - Europe's Foreign and Security Policies, DAFF 25A92 - The European Union as an Area of Freedom, Security and Justice, DSPO 25A13 - Decision-Making Process of the European Union: an insider’s view (The)
Jeg skulle have 3 kurser på 15 ECTS i alt for at få forhåndsgodkendt Europæisk Politik på 7,5 ECTS:
DAFF 25A65 - Europe's Foreign and Security Policies, DAFF 25A92 - The European Union as an Area of Freedom, Security and Justice, DSPO 25A13 - Decision-Making Process of the European Union: an insider’s view (The)
Be aware that the teacher in DSPO 25A13 - Decision-Making Process of the European Union: an insider’s view (The) retires in the summer of 2024 and therefore his course cannot be chosen in E2024 and onwards and thus there is one less course to choose among the Europæisk politik kurser when applying for forhåndsgodkendelse fra a UCPH point of view.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
All courses by Jean-Yves Haine:
ASPO 25A23 - International Wars and Conflicts, DAFF 25A65 - Europe's Foreign and Security Policies
I chose all the courses this guy taught based on a previous review here and it was the best decision ever. "This guy is the best professor I've ever had. His knowledge is so thorough and his reasoning so clear. Very good at explaining very complex issues, cases and subjects and giving historical examples. Very good at connecting the dots and giving critical assessments. This course was a real eye opener for me and I was sad when it finished. I also loved the form of examination being a lot more about independent argumentation and reasoning not bound to the syllabus rather than the traditional way of remembering facts by heart and focussing on syllabus. His way I think is a lot more useful."
He is brilliant at critical thinking and reasoning, explaining great details by example and also the broad strokes. His classes are just him talking in 2 hours which for most would be very boring, but not him. The way he thinks is out of the box and extraordinary. I've never been so amazed and star struck by a professor. It is not about who said what but about understanding the ways of interaction among states and their actors. Also his way of examination and assignments is: "fuck the syllabus and readings and learning by heart, what are your opinions and can you make a good and clear argument?" Unfortunately he also teaches in Rome so he is not always teaching in Paris and therefore you may not be able to choose him. Also he was the one in charge to chart the foreign policy of not just France, but the whole of the EU some years back. Check out his credentials, they are amazing. Also he is very nice and sweet and you feel very comfortable being around him. A bit like a grandfather-ish energy.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were in general more expensive than Copenhagen, but some things are cheaper. A solution is to eat as many meals as possible at CROUS restaurants where you can eat for 3,3 € for a full meal or just 1 € if you go to CROUS at Mabillion (3 Rue Mabillon, 75006 Paris) during their opening hours to get an IZLY card (meal card to pay for meals). If it is the right lady (thin, young and African decent who only speaks French) sitting there on the ground floor reception your Erasmus grant will qualify you to the 1 € meal since you'll be regarded as a "boursier". I found out by sheer luck and got the 1 € meal. But most other places don't offer this 1 € meal to Erasmus students. I ate this 1 € meal two times a day (2 times a day is the limit, the rest cost 3,3 €) every weekday and this was half of the times sufficient for me. The rest I would eat "Fromage Blanc", very cheap healthy and tasty since it is not as sour as normal Danish yoghurt. I only needed to cook for the weekends and holidays. Therefore I lived for less than 1000 DKK per month which would have been impossible in Denmark. I didn't go out to eat at all though. The food was the best and most healthy I've eaten as a student since I could pick fish at CROUS for nearly every single meal. A lot of vegetables as well and nearly no processed food, mostly home-made. You can also go to eat at CROUS without an IZLY card, but then you'll have to pay 3,3 € if you can show your student card. Also you can buy your meal take away with no extra surcharge if you say "importer". Also if you're not full yet you can grab your empty plate and go back in and say "Du Rab" to get a free refill of the starch and veggies but without the meat (only at CROUS Mabillion and not CROUS Cité Universitaire). Also there are cakes and sandwiches, all non-profit and very much state subsidised especially the 1 € meal since it is CROUS. CROUS restaurants/cafeteria is probably one of the best parts of studying in France since we don't have this in Denmark at all. The queues can be a bit long though, but hey it would have taken longer time to buy the groceries, cook and wash the dishes and a lot more expensive. Also you can get free travel insurance through a Norwegian Bank credit card which I did. Otherwise the blue EU health insurance card should be sufficient, since you pay the same going to the doctor as the French. You also don't need to buy a sim-card since roaming for 4 months is totally fine and free without any warnings or issues (I use Telmore). No book purchases are required at Sciences Po therefore 0 DKK. Also check out APL from CAF, it is like boligstøtte and you're eligible being an EU citizen albeit it takes a very long time and everything is in French and very bureaucratic. For transportation I just rented a Swapfiets bike for 21 € with student discount which was the cheapest option, but biking in Paris is a nightmare. I didn't buy anything or spent money on any tickets because most attractions such as museums are free if you're under 26 from the EU. The flight tickets to Paris are more expensive than I imagined so remember to buy them as early as possible. I had to pay around 1000 DKK one way to go to Paris with a checked in suitcase. Also the public transport is less expensive than Copenhagen. The Ile de France ticket monthly ticket for adults is around the same as the price of a ungdomskort in Copenhagen, but going to the airport without a monthly/weekly ticket is way more expensive than Copenhagen. Also there is a 1 year ticket for students for 365 € so if you're staying here for longer than 4 months it could be worth it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't attend any so I cannot review this, but they have a lot of different scheduled activities and loads of one-off talks etc. Everything will be sent to your Sciences Po e-mail as newsletters.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: https://www.sciencespo.fr/en/life-at-sciences-po/culture-athletics-and-associations/

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Going to the museums/palaces for free if you're under 26. Paris is probably the city in Europe with most attractions and things to see and do. Check out the huge amount of free activities at Cité Universitaire even if you're not a resident you can join all the public stuff such as concerts, opera, theatre, book talks, dances, parkour, movie screenings etc. Baguette is always good and cheap, but remember to buy them fresh. Go to the bakery and try their pink equivalent to kanelsnegl, they are fantastic. Also French food in general is way superior to Danish food so try out: cheese such as Comté with fig jam, all their tarts, eclair, all their fruits and vegetables tastes a lot better than the ones in Denmark since they are more ripe/have had more sun, e.g. their apples actually taste good! Also appreciate the much milder and warmer weather, the longer days during the Autumn since Paris is to the west, but in the same time zone as Denmark, which extends the possibilities of doing activities outdoors. Even in December the sun first sets at 17:00.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See above. Day trip to Versailles + Trianon & Fontainebleau all free for youth under 26.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: In between I would say. Probably a lot easier than going outside of Western Europe, but still quite different from Denmark. The French love to comment and "stikke næsen i alting". And there is so many rules and documentation/bureaucracy needed everywhere and much is still written in paper and not online. Thus much less digitalised than Denmark. But the French are also more open to foreigners than Danes and it is more easy to become friends with the locals than in Denmark. Paris is very international so the local culture was not only the French, but people from all around the world especially at Sciences Po and Cité Universitaire.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just go to CROUS restaurants and talk to the people sitting next to you. This is OK in Paris even though it may feel intimidating as a Dane, since we usually keep to ourselves at home. But it is totally worth it. You'll be amazed of how diverse people you'll meet there. I got several local friends this way and even more international friends. Befriending local students at Sciences Po is way harder since they usually don't take courses in English and thus you don't get to meet them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
On top of the heavy air pollution: Smoking/vaping everywhere outside, in every courtyard, street etc. also at Sciences Po. This is Denmark 20 years ago. Nobody cares about passive smoking and none have heard about bagged nicotine you can put in your mouth and not bother others (quite popular in Denmark among the youth). I'm not a smoker and I hated this
Also a lot less recycling and sorting waste.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: See above. Also: The Parisian women dress so well, especially around Sciences Po. I cannot summarise it with words but they love their trench coats, pantyhose/stockings and high heeled boots. Their style and fashion is some of the best I've seen and feels so effortless and understated yet chic. It is not about bright colours and prints but well tailored pieces in uniform colours. Very inspiring. I feel they are next level compared to us Danes and we're very underdressed.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Cheap and healthy meals at CROUS restaurants with loads of opportunities at meeting others
Fantastic academic opportunities and variety of quality courses at Sciences Po Paris with small classes and lots of money and resources to back it up.
Lots to see and do in Paris most of which is free when under 26

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: See above

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being able to live by myself while managing to complete the 2x workload compared to UCPH. Trying the "Sciences Po approach" of teaching which I really liked compared to UCPH. Being able to talk to so many different people especially at CROUS restaurants. I've never met so many nationalities before, I've talked to people from all around the world and the international perspective of Paris is probably unmatched in Europe besides London.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding a place to live. Managing my time with the double workload and frequent deadlines compared to UCPH. Missing my partner back home in Denmark.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
